title: Worksheet — Grassroots Democracy: Governance (Class 6 CBSE Social Science)
instructions: Attempt all 11 questions. Show your reasoning where required. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: The way a community organises itself to take decisions and get things done is called:
The word 'democracy' comes from Greek words meaning:
India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.
The voting age in India is ____ years.
Which subject is mainly handled by the LOCAL government?
The 73rd and 74th Amendments to the Constitution were passed in:
List four features of a democracy.
questions.answer: (i) People CHOOSE their rulers in fair elections. (ii) Every adult has ONE vote of equal value. (iii) Different parties and candidates can compete. (iv) The ruler's power is LIMITED by laws and a Constitution. (Also: citizens have rights the ruler cannot take away.)

questions.question: What do the words SOVEREIGN, SECULAR and REPUBLIC mean in the Preamble of our Constitution?
questions.answer: SOVEREIGN — independent; no foreign country tells India what to do. SECULAR — the state has no official religion; all religions are treated equally. REPUBLIC — the head of state (the President) is elected, not a hereditary king.

questions.question: Match each subject to the level of government most responsible: (a) defence, (b) state police, (c) village street lights, (d) currency.
questions.answer: (a) defence — Union. (b) state police — State. (c) village street lights — Local. (d) currency — Union.

questions.question: Compare a kingdom and a democracy on the three big questions: WHO rules, HOW decisions are made, and HOW power is limited.
questions.answer: WHO rules: in a kingdom, ONE person (the king) rules, usually by birth; in a democracy, the PEOPLE rule through elected representatives. HOW decisions are made: in a kingdom, by orders from the king; in a democracy, by discussion in assemblies, voting and laws made through Parliament. HOW power is limited: in a kingdom, the king's power is often unlimited; in a democracy, the ruler's power is limited by a written Constitution, by independent courts, by elections, and by citizens' rights even the ruler cannot take away.

questions.question: A village's well has been broken for two months. Why is the LOCAL government the best level to fix this problem? Use the ideas of GRAM SWARAJ and the 73rd Amendment in your answer.
questions.answer: The Union and State governments are far away — they cannot easily know that a particular well in a particular village is broken or which families it serves. The LOCAL Panchayat is closest to the people: it lives with the problem, can inspect it the same day, and can call the gram sabha to decide. Gandhi's idea of GRAM SWARAJ — village self-rule — argues that strong villages make a strong India, with each village solving its own problems. The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave Panchayats a constitutional foundation, regular elections, reserved seats for women / SCs / STs and clear powers, including over local water and sanitation. So fixing the well is exactly the kind of task local government was designed for.
